note: Phase 1 starter set. Every quote below was checked against a primary or clearly documented secondary source before inclusion — nothing here was generated because it 'sounded right'. Coverage is intentionally partial: only concepts/themes with quotes I could verify are included. More will be added in later passes rather than padded out now.

quotes.quote: Constitutional morality is not a natural sentiment. It has to be cultivated. We must realize that our people have yet to learn it.
quotes.author: B. R. Ambedkar
quotes.source: Speech to the Constituent Assembly, 4 November 1948
quotes.meaning: Ambedkar warned that following a democratic constitution's forms and spirit does not come naturally to a society — it has to be consciously learned and practised.
quotes.usage: Use when a question asks about constitutional values, the gap between law and practice, or why constitutionalism needs civic education.

quotes.quote: A paramount reverence for the forms of the constitution, enforcing obedience to authority and acting under and within these forms, yet combined with the habit of open speech, of action subject only to definite legal control, and unrestrained censure of those very authorities as to all their public acts.
quotes.author: B. R. Ambedkar
quotes.source: Speech to the Constituent Assembly, 4 November 1948 (quoting George Grote's definition, which Ambedkar endorsed)
quotes.meaning: Defines constitutional morality as obeying constitutional forms while still retaining the right to freely criticise those in authority.
quotes.usage: Good for a body paragraph on dissent, free speech and constitutionalism coexisting.

quotes.quote: An honest public servant can't become rich in politics. He can only attain greatness and satisfaction by service.
quotes.author: Harry S. Truman
quotes.source: Widely documented in Truman's public remarks; commonly cited in public-service literature
quotes.meaning: Public office should be measured by service rendered, not personal enrichment.
quotes.usage: Use for questions on integrity, probity, or why public servants shouldn't use office for personal gain.

quotes.quote: Public service must be more than doing a job efficiently and honestly. It must be a complete dedication to the people and to the nation.
quotes.author: Margaret Chase Smith
quotes.source: U.S. Senator; widely documented public remarks
quotes.meaning: Competence and honesty are necessary but not sufficient — service requires genuine commitment.
quotes.usage: Useful to distinguish 'efficiency' from 'dedication' in a governance or civil-service answer.

quotes.quote: A public office is not a job, it is an opportunity to do something for the public.
quotes.author: Franklin Knight Lane
quotes.source: U.S. Secretary of the Interior; widely documented public remarks
quotes.meaning: Reframes public office as an opportunity for service rather than a career transaction.
quotes.usage: Short, quotable line — works well as an opening or closing line on the civil-services/GS4 theme.

quotes.quote: Supposing I have come by a fair amount of wealth — either by way of legacy, or by means of trade and industry — I must know that all that wealth does not belong to me; what belongs to me is the right to an honourable livelihood, no better than that enjoyed by millions of others. The rest of my wealth belongs to the community and must be used for the welfare of the community.
quotes.author: Mahatma Gandhi
quotes.source: Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi, on the doctrine of Trusteeship
quotes.meaning: Gandhi's Trusteeship doctrine: wealth and power are held in trust for society, not owned absolutely.
quotes.usage: Strong for essays/GS4 answers on inequality, CSR, or the ethics of wealth and power.

quotes.quote: The man, then, who faces and who fears the right things and from the right motive, in the right way and at the right time, and who feels confidence under the corresponding conditions, is brave; for the brave man feels and acts according to the merits of the case and in whatever way the rule directs.
quotes.author: Aristotle
quotes.source: Nicomachean Ethics, Book III (W. D. Ross translation)
quotes.meaning: Courage is a mean between rashness and cowardice — feeling the right fear, for the right reason, at the right time.
quotes.usage: Use for GS4 questions distinguishing courage from recklessness, e.g. in whistleblowing or crisis-decision case studies.

quotes.quote: Good governance is ensuring respect for human rights and the rule of law; strengthening democracy; promoting transparency and capacity in public administration.
quotes.author: Kofi Annan
quotes.source: UN Secretary-General; documented public remarks (Kofi Annan Foundation)
quotes.meaning: Ties transparency and accountability directly to the definition of good governance.
quotes.usage: Use for GS2/GS4 questions on accountability mechanisms, RTI, or e-governance.

quotes.quote: Artificial intelligence is likely to be either the best or worst thing to happen to humanity.
quotes.author: Stephen Hawking
quotes.source: Public remarks, widely reported (BBC, NBC News, c. 2014-2016)
quotes.meaning: Frames AI as a genuine double-edged development, not simply progress or simply danger.
quotes.usage: Strong opening line for a technology/AI essay — sets up a balanced two-sided argument.

quotes.quote: We need to be super careful with AI. Potentially more dangerous than nukes.
quotes.author: Elon Musk
quotes.meaning: A blunt warning about the scale of risk unregulated AI development could pose.
quotes.usage: Use to introduce the 'risk/regulation' dimension of a technology essay.

quotes.quote: The 'control of nature' is a phrase conceived in arrogance, born of the Neanderthal age of biology and philosophy, when it was supposed that nature exists for the convenience of man.
quotes.author: Rachel Carson
quotes.meaning: Critiques the assumption that nature exists to be dominated and used by humans without consequence.
quotes.usage: Powerful for essays on development-vs-environment trade-offs or the ethics of exploiting nature.

quotes.quote: In this now universal contamination of the environment, chemicals are the sinister and little-recognized partners of radiation in changing the very nature of the world — the very nature of its life.
quotes.author: Rachel Carson
quotes.meaning: Highlights how slow, invisible environmental damage can be as consequential as dramatic disasters.
quotes.usage: Good for essays on pollution, climate change, or the invisibility of ecological harm.

quotes.quote: Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela
quotes.source: Speech at Madison Park High School, Boston, 23 June 1990 (exact phrasing varies slightly across press reports of the period)
quotes.meaning: Positions education as the primary lever for social transformation.
quotes.usage: Classic, well-known opening or closing line for essays on education, empowerment or social change — because it's so widely used, pair it with a less obvious point to avoid a generic-sounding essay.

quotes.quote: Good governance is ensuring respect for human rights and the rule of law; strengthening democracy; promoting transparency and capacity in public administration.
quotes.author: Kofi Annan
quotes.meaning: A working definition of good governance tying together rights, democracy and transparency.
quotes.usage: Useful anchor definition for a governance essay's introduction.

quotes.quote: Long years ago, we made a tryst with destiny, and now the time comes when we shall redeem our pledge, not wholly or in full measure, but very substantially. At the stroke of the midnight hour, when the world sleeps, India will awake to life and freedom.
quotes.author: Jawaharlal Nehru
quotes.source: 'Tryst with Destiny' speech to the Constituent Assembly, midnight of 14-15 August 1947
quotes.meaning: Marks India's independence as the fulfilment of a long, collective national pledge.
quotes.usage: Use for essays on nationhood, independence, or India's civilisational journey — best in the introduction, given how well-known it is.

quotes.quote: A moment comes, which comes but rarely in history, when we step out from the old to the new, when an age ends, and when the soul of a nation, long suppressed, finds utterance.
quotes.author: Jawaharlal Nehru
quotes.meaning: Frames independence as a civilisational turning point, not just a political event.
quotes.usage: Works well for essays on transformation, historical turning points, or national identity.
